tools.description: List the research methods this workspace can run — with the exact stimulus fields each one requires — plus remaining plan headroom and simulation-session balance. Call this before thesia_run_study or thesia_test_copy to pick a method and check cost headroom. Everything Thesia runs is a SIMULATION of a simulated audience, not real-user research.

section.description: 'methods' lists the research methods available and the inputs each needs. 'limits' returns just your remaining plan headroom and session balance. Default 'all'.

tools.name: thesia_list_capabilities
tools.title: List what you can run and what plan headroom is left

tools.description: Quote how many simulation sessions a run would cost, and roughly what share of your plan it would consume, before committing to it. Free — this never starts a simulation. Use it to size an audience or shorten a study when headroom is tight.

kind.description: What you are about to run.

method.description: Required when kind is 'study' — the research method id.

variants.description: Number of message variants, for a copy test or a study that compares variants (messaging_test). Every variant is simulated by every respondent, so cost scales with it. Defaults to 2, the minimum.

tools.name: thesia_estimate

sessions.description: Estimated simulation sessions, or null when Thesia cannot quote this kind up front. Never treat null as zero — read `note` instead.

tools.title: Estimate the cost of a simulation before running it

tools.description: Give Thesia a decision you need to make, in plain English, and it designs the study, picks or builds the audience, prices it, and runs it — then writes a decision brief. Use this when you do not already know which research method fits; use thesia_run_study when you do. It can also simulate a whole funnel (an ad leading to a landing page, and which call to action people take there): describe the ad, the page URL and the goals in the objective. It always stops for your approval at a price before spending anything: expect status 'needs_price_confirmation' and answer it with thesia_confirm_study. Call it again with autopilot_id to check on a plan already running. Results are SIMULATED predicted behaviour, not real-user research.

asset_ids.description: Optional. Ids of ads the user already uploaded to Thesia (images or videos). Pass them when the objective is about those ads, e.g. a funnel: 'our Instagram ad leads to example.com/offer; do people book a call or use the plan form?'.

audience_id.description: Optional saved audience pack / persona group id (UUID) to draw the sample from.

autopilot_id.description: Check an existing plan instead of starting one. Mutually exclusive with objective.

max_wait_seconds.description: How long to wait inline before handing back an id. Defaults to 45.

objective.description: What you need to decide, in plain English — e.g. 'should we price the starter plan at 29 or 49 for early-stage dev teams?'. Starts a new plan. Omit when checking an existing one.

tools.name: thesia_plan_study

status.description: 'running' | 'needs_price_confirmation' | 'needs_clarification' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'cancelled'. The two 'needs_' values are states with a concrete next action, not failures.

tools.title: Plan and run a study from a plain-English objective

tools.description: Respond to a plan from thesia_plan_study. Use action 'confirm' with accept_sessions to approve the quoted cost and start the run — this is the point at which simulation sessions are spent, so check with the user first. Use 'answer' to reply to the clarifying questions (answers with the option ids the user picked, or answer for one free-text reply), 'cancel' to abandon the plan, or 'retry' after a failure. After confirming, the run continues and returns its decision brief when it finishes.

accept_sessions.description: Required for 'confirm': the exact sessions figure from the plan's estimate. Never invent it — a mismatch is rejected and re-quoted.

action.description: 'confirm' accepts the quoted cost and starts the run (requires accept_sessions). 'answer' replies to the clarifying questions (requires answers or answer). 'cancel' abandons the plan. 'retry' re-runs a failed plan.

answer.description: For 'answer': a free-text reply to the (first) question asked. Prefer answers when the plan lists questions.

answers.description: For 'answer': one entry per question from the plan's questions, with the optionId the user picked or their own text. A question left out keeps its default. Only relay what the user said.

optionId.description: The id of the option the user picked.

questionId.description: A question id from the plan's questions.

text.description: The user's own words, when no option fits.

max_wait_seconds.description: How long to wait inline after confirming before handing back an id. Defaults to 45.

tools.name: thesia_confirm_study

requiredSessions.description: Set only on a re-quote — confirm this figure instead.

tools.title: Approve, answer, cancel or retry a planned study

tools.description: Instant read. Reads 2-5 variants against a census-weighted simulated population for a market, in seconds, and returns each variant's predicted action propensity, its lift over the control, and which demographic archetypes favour it. A variant can be copy (text), a live page (url), or an image (image_url or image_base64). Image reads are single-kind: images cannot be mixed with copy or pages. For a video, use thesia_pretest_video. The first read of a new image takes about 30-45 s and may come back running (collect it with thesia_get_result). Much cheaper and faster than thesia_test_copy, which is the deeper follow-up. Counts against the monthly read allowance, not simulation sessions. Results are SIMULATED, not real-user data.

audience.description: Read against a saved audience (persona group id from thesia_list_audiences) instead of a market.

market.description: Who to read against, as a place: 'United States', 'Germany', 'RO'. Defaults to the US.

target_action.description: The action the variants should drive, e.g. 'Sign up'.

title.description: Optional name for the read in your run history.

variants.description: 2-5 variants to read side by side. Images and videos are read on their own, not mixed with other kinds.

is_control.description: The current/baseline variant. Exactly one; defaults to the first.

label.description: Optional short name for this variant.

url.description: A live page to read, http or https.

where.description: Where the variants appear. Defaults to 'Landing page'.

tools.name: thesia_read
tools.title: Instant read: which variant lands with a market

tools.description: Run a Research Lab study — pricing sensitivity, message testing, concept testing, focus groups — against a simulated audience and get a structured verdict with segment breakdowns, objections and representative reactions. Call thesia_list_capabilities first to pick a method and see the inputs it needs. Results are SIMULATED predicted behaviour, not feedback from real users.

accept_sessions.description: Only needed after a 'needs_price_confirmation' result. Pass back the exact requiredSessions value from that response to proceed.

audience.description: Optional saved audience (persona group) id to draw the sample from. Omit to draw from your existing simulated audience.

audience_size.description: Simulated respondents. Defaults to the method's own default (usually 30). Drives cost.

depth.description: How deeply each respondent engages. Cost multiplier: single_pass 1x, deliberation 2x, deep 4x.

hypothesis.description: Optional. What you expect to find.

market.description: Optional. Country the respondents must live in, e.g. 'RO' or 'Romania'. Only personas there are sampled; when the workspace has too few, nothing runs or bills and the result is 'needs_audience'. Ignored when 'audience' names a saved audience.

max_wait_seconds.description: How long to wait inline before handing back an id to poll. Defaults to 45.

method.description: Research method id, from thesia_list_capabilities — e.g. 'messaging_test', 'concept_test', 'feature_adoption', 'pricing_van_westendorp', 'focus_group'.

objective.description: The decision this study should inform.

regulated.description: Optional. True for regulated sectors (claims are checked).

scenario.description: Optional emotional condition from the method's supportedConditions, e.g. 'budget_anxiety'.

stimulus.description: The method's own stimulus fields, keyed by the `key` values in that method's stimulusSchema (see thesia_list_capabilities). A variant_list field takes an array of { text, isControl } objects, 2-5 entries.

title.description: Short name for this study, e.g. 'Q3 pricing band for Pro'.

tools.name: thesia_run_study

matchedPersonas.description: On 'needs_audience' for a market: personas found in that market.

requestedPersonas.description: On 'needs_audience' for a market: respondents the study needs.

sample.description: Who answered: people vs responses and where they live.

sessionsConsumed.description: Simulation sessions billed to this run.

tools.title: Run a research study with a simulated audience

tools.description: Compare 2-5 copy variants — headlines, value propositions, ad or email copy — against a simulated audience, and get a ranked verdict with predicted action propensity, comprehension and trust per variant, plus the objections each raises. Results are SIMULATED predicted reactions, not feedback from real users.

accept_sessions.description: Only after a 'needs_price_confirmation' result: the exact requiredSessions value from that response, re-sent to authorize the spend. Never guess it.

audience.description: Optional saved audience (persona group) id to test against.

max_wait_seconds.description: How long to wait inline before handing back an id to poll. Defaults to 45.

objective.description: What this copy should achieve, e.g. 'get developers to start a free trial'.

target_action.description: The action the copy should drive.

is_control.description: Mark the current/baseline copy. Exactly one variant should be the control.

label.description: Optional short name for this variant.

text.description: One message variant — a headline, value proposition, or short copy block.

tools.name: thesia_test_copy
tools.title: Test copy variants against a simulated audience

tools.description: Run a behavioral simulation of one page: simulated visitors from a simulated audience tour the page and report where they hesitate, get confused or drop off, with concrete fixes and messaging-clarity findings. Useful for checking a freshly built or changed page. Results are SIMULATED (predicted behavior of a simulated audience), not feedback from real users.

audience.description: Optional. A simulated audience to use: a persona id or name from thesia_list_audiences, or a short free-text description (e.g. 'first-time SaaS buyers'). If omitted, Thesia simulates a small mixed audience.

focus.description: Optional. What to pay attention to, e.g. 'checkout flow', 'onboarding clarity', 'is the value proposition clear?'.

max_wait_seconds.description: How long to wait inline before handing back an id to poll. Defaults to 45.

num_agents.description: How many simulated visitors walk the page. Default 3. Drives cost — quote it with thesia_estimate (kind 'audit', audience_size = this number) before raising it.

objective.description: Optional. What you want to find out, in your own words, e.g. 'how do new users feel about our onboarding flow?'. Sent as written (not paraphrased); steers the simulated visitors and the report.

scope.description: Optional. Where visitors may go: 'page' (the url only, the default), 'path' (a subtree, value '/blog') or 'site' (the whole domain).

value.description: For 'path': a subtree like '/blog'. For 'page': a path or full URL.

url.description: The full URL of the page to audit (e.g. https://example.com/pricing).

tools.name: thesia_audit_site

next.description: Suggested next action when status is 'running'.

status.description: 'completed' when findings are inline, or 'running' when pollable.

tools.title: Audit a site with a simulated audience

tools.description: SECONDARY TOOL. Pose a question to a SINGLE simulated persona and get one predicted, in-character response — good for an open-ended 'would this confuse someone like this?' sounding-out. The answer is SIMULATED (one persona's predicted reaction), not a real person, and ONE persona is not an audience: it carries no distribution and no disagreement, so never report it as what 'users' or 'the audience' think. For a finding you can act on, use thesia_test_copy (compare variants) or thesia_run_study / thesia_plan_study (a panel with a spread of reactions).

audience.description: Optional. A persona id or name from thesia_list_audiences to answer as. If omitted, one of your simulated audiences is chosen automatically.

context.description: Optional. Background/situation for the audience to consider when answering.

language.description: Optional. The language to answer in, e.g. 'English' or 'Romanian'. Personas answer in their own native language by default, which is correct for research but unreadable when you asked in another language. Set this to your own language unless you specifically want the persona's.

question.description: The question to ask the simulated audience (e.g. 'Would this pricing page confuse you?').

tools.name: thesia_ask_audience
tools.title: Ask ONE simulated persona a question (secondary)

tools.description: Run a post (X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook) or email through a simulated audience and get predicted engagement, sentiment and representative reactions before publishing. Starts the run and waits briefly; collect with thesia_get_result kind 'post_simulation'. Results are SIMULATED reactions, not real engagement.

accept_sessions.description: Only after a 'needs_price_confirmation' result: the exact requiredSessions value from it, re-sent to authorize the spend. Never guess it.

audience_size.description: Simulated audience members. Default 100. Drives cost.

image_url.description: Public URL of an image attached to the post, if any.

link_url.description: Link attached to the post, if any.

objective.description: What the post is for, e.g. 'drive webinar signups'.

persona_ids.description: Specific personas (from thesia_list_audiences) to use. Omit to use the workspace pool.

text.description: The post (or email body) exactly as it would be published.

tone.description: Tone of the simulated comments. Default balanced.

tools.name: thesia_simulate_post
tools.title: Simulate how an audience reacts to a post

tools.description: Stop a study, instant read, plan, audit or post simulation that is still running. Use it when the user changes their mind or a run was started with the wrong inputs. Finished runs are not affected.

id.description: run_id for a study or read, autopilotId for a plan, job_id for an audit, or the post simulation id.

kind.description: The kind named in the run tool's response.

tools.name: thesia_cancel
tools.title: Cancel a running Thesia run

tools.description: List the workspace's recent simulations across studies, instant reads, plans, audits and post simulations, newest first, with the kind and id to pass to thesia_get_result or thesia_get_brief. Use it to find earlier work instead of re-running it. Page back with 'before' (or bound by 'after'). Lists only the signed-in account's workspace: runs made under another sign-in or API key are in that account.

after.description: Only runs created on or after this date (ISO, e.g. '2026-11-13').

before.description: Only runs created before this date or time (ISO, e.g. '2026-11-20' or a createdAt from an earlier page). Use it to page back through history.

kind.description: Only this kind of run. Default 'all'. Studies include copy tests and instant reads.

tools.name: thesia_list_runs

nextBefore.description: Pass as 'before' to get the next, older page.

workspaceId.description: The workspace these runs belong to. Runs made under another sign-in or API key are not listed.

tools.title: List recent Thesia runs

tools.description: Fetch the findings of a run started by thesia_run_study, thesia_test_copy, thesia_audit_site, thesia_plan_study, thesia_read, thesia_simulate_post, thesia_compare_creatives or thesia_pretest_video, using the kind and id from that tool's response. Simulations run longer than a single tool call, so this is the normal way to collect results. All results are SIMULATED predicted behaviour, not real-user data.

id.description: The id from the run tool — job_id for audits, run_id for studies and copy tests, autopilotId for plans, the simulation id for a post simulation, the comparisonId for a creative comparison, or the experimentId for a video analysis.

kind.description: Which kind of run to fetch. Use the kind named in the run tool's `next` hint.

tools.name: thesia_get_result

sample.description: Who answered: people vs responses and where they live.

tools.title: Get the result of a Thesia run

tools.description: Fetch the result of an audit started by thesia_audit_site, using its job_id. Returns the full simulated behavioral findings once complete, or a 'running' status to poll again. Results are SIMULATED predicted behavior, not real users.

include.description: Extra detail to fetch alongside the report. 'journeys' is the step-by-step path each simulated visitor took; 'heatmap' is where attention landed per page. Both are large — ask for them only when the summary is not enough to answer the question.

job_id.description: The job_id returned by thesia_audit_site (or an audit report id).

tools.name: thesia_get_audit_result
tools.title: Get the result of a simulated-audience audit

tools.description: Turn a finished study, audit, read or post simulation into a short decision brief: the question, a direct answer, the reasoning with supporting simulated reactions, the risks, and what to do next. This is what you hand a human — use it instead of relaying raw metrics. Reuses the stored brief when one exists, so repeat calls are free (unless language, register or regulated is given: that writes a new brief with a model call). Everything in it comes from SIMULATED behaviour, not real-user research.

id.description: The run id for a study, or the reportId (not the job_id) for an audit.

kind.description: 'study' for a run_study / test_copy / plan_study / read run id, 'audit' for an audit report id, 'post_simulation' for a simulate_post id.

language.description: Optional. Brief language (e.g. 'ro'); sent as reportLanguage.

regenerate.description: Re-write a brief that already exists. Costs another model call — leave unset to reuse the stored one. Passing language, register or regulated also writes a new brief.

register.description: Optional. Tone register of the brief.

regulated.description: Optional. Set true for regulated sectors (claims are checked).

tools.name: thesia_get_brief
tools.title: Get the plain-language decision brief for a finished run

tools.description: Mint a shareable URL for a completed study, audit or creative comparison so someone without a Thesia account can read the findings. Use it after thesia_get_brief when the user wants to send the results to a colleague or client, or post them. The link is PUBLIC to anyone who has it. A study shared without options gets its public link plus a preview card for posting; pass expires_in or a password for a private, expiring link instead.

expires_in.description: How long the link stays live. Audits and comparisons default to 30d. A study with no expiry and no password gets its public link (stays live until the owner stops sharing it).

id.description: The run id for a study, the reportId (not the job_id) for an audit, or the comparison id.

kind.description: 'study' for a research run id, 'audit' for an audit report id, 'creative_comparison' for a compare_creatives comparison id.

password.description: Optional password required to open the link. Never returned in the response.

tools.name: thesia_share_result
tools.title: Create a public link to a finished run's findings

tools.description: Assemble a markdown pretest report (how we worked, one section per set, what the results mean, sealed predictions appendix) from finished simulations. Deterministic unless generateFixes is true (then the model drafts fixes and a one-line summary per set, if enabled on the account); otherwise the recommended fixes are left as placeholders for the analyst. Returns the markdown plus claim-lint warnings to resolve before sending. Seals each set's prediction as a side effect. Results are simulated, not real-user data. For a branded PDF, open the same report in the app at /dashboard/ad-lab/pretest and use Download PDF.

generateFixes.description: Ask the model to draft 3-5 concrete fixes and a one-line summary per set. Default false.

regulated.description: True for regulated sectors; claims are linted harder.

sets.description: 1-12 finished runs, one report section each.

assumptions.description: Assumptions to state in this set's section.

id.description: Comparison, video analysis or research run id.

kind.description: Which kind of finished run this set is.

tools.name: thesia_pretest_report
tools.title: Build a pretest report

tools.description: Compare 2+ image creatives (thumbnails, display banners, social images) against a simulated audience. Creates the experiment, uploads the images, attaches the audience and drafts the comparison (free). It then returns status 'needs_price_confirmation' with the quoted simulation sessions; nothing is spent until you re-call with accept_sessions >= the quote (pass accept_sessions up front to skip the pause). To confirm a draft already created, pass comparison_id + accept_sessions only. Cost scales with creatives x personas; an audience group is capped at 10 personas per segment. choice_task adds a forced-choice round (choiceCost in the quote). Collect the ranking with thesia_get_result kind 'creative_comparison'. Results are simulated, not real-user data.

accept_sessions.description: Sessions you accept to spend; must cover the quote.

choice_task.description: Also run a forced-choice task (each persona picks one creative). Adds sessions; the quote shows choiceCost.

comparison_id.description: Confirm and run a draft created by an earlier call.

creatives.description: 2-10 creatives to compare. Needed unless you pass comparison_id.

body.description: Body copy shown with the image.

concept.description: Creatives sharing a concept are grouped; the first is its representative.

persona_ids.description: Persona ids (see thesia_list_audiences), instead of an audience group.

tools.name: thesia_compare_creatives
tools.title: Compare image creatives

tools.description: Pretest a short video (mp4, mov, webm; max 512 MB, 10 minutes) against a simulated audience: hook score, attention curve, drop-off points. Uploads the file (from video_url), splits it into scenes, then returns status 'needs_price_confirmation' with the quote. The quote exists only after preparing, and the draft is free EXCEPT speech-to-text: when you pass no transcript_srt, preparing charges 0.25 to 6 simulation sessions for transcription up front. Analysis cost is personas x 5 + scenes x 0.5 sessions, minimum 10, max 60 personas. Nothing more is spent until you re-call with accept_sessions >= the quote (pass it up front to skip the pause). If preparing is still running the tool returns 'preparing' with experiment_id, video_id and prepare_job_id: call again with those. Collect with thesia_get_result kind 'video_analysis'. Results are simulated, not real-user data.

accept_sessions.description: Sessions you accept to spend; must cover the quote.

hook_windows.description: Split scenes into hook windows so the opening seconds are scored on their own. Default true.

persona_ids.description: Persona ids, instead of an audience group.

segments.description: Limit an audience group to these segment ids.

transcript_srt.description: SRT transcript; skips the speech-to-text charge.

video_url.description: http(s) link to a video file.

tools.name: thesia_pretest_video
tools.title: Pretest a video

tools.description: Lock a prediction (a creative comparison ranking, a video analysis, a study or a manual payload) with a SHA-256 hash and timestamp, so it can later be compared with what really happened. Pass source_id to seal a finished simulation, or payload for a manual prediction. Returns the id, hash and sealed payload.

source_id.description: Id of the comparison, video analysis or study run.

tools.name: thesia_seal_prediction
tools.title: Seal a prediction before the outcome is known

tools.description: Recompute the hash of a sealed prediction and report whether it still matches the stored one.
tools.name: thesia_verify_prediction
tools.title: Verify a sealed prediction

tools.description: Attach what actually happened to a sealed prediction (append-only) and get the evaluation. creative_comparison actual: {metric:'ctr', values:[{creativeId?|variant?, value, impressions?, clicks?}]}; impressions and clicks let Thesia record the result for calibration (see calibrationRecorded). video_analysis actual: {threeSecondHoldPct?, biggestDropSec?, watchedFullPct?}. Other kinds: any object.

note.description: Optional free-text note stored with the outcome.

source.description: Where the numbers came from, e.g. 'client_email_2026-10-09'.

tools.name: thesia_record_outcome
tools.title: Record the real outcome of a sealed prediction

tools.description: Create a secret upload link to send a client so they can drop creative files (images, video) for pretesting. Returns the url and expiry; treat the url as a secret and share it only with the client. Needs a workspace admin or manager, and the feature must be enabled for the workspace (otherwise a clear 'not enabled' message).

expires_in_days.description: Days until the link expires (1-30, default 14).

label.description: Who or what the link is for, e.g. 'Acme spring banners'.

max_total_mb.description: Max total size in MB (default and cap 2048).

tools.name: thesia_create_intake_link
tools.title: Create a client file-intake link

tools.description: List the files a client uploaded through an intake link (name, type, size, status, set label, a short-lived download url). The feature must be enabled for the workspace.
tools.name: thesia_list_intake_files
tools.title: List files uploaded through an intake link

tools.description: List the simulated audiences (simulated personas) in this workspace: their overall shape (where they are, what they do, how much is actually filled in) plus a sample with ids. These are simulated personas, not real people, and a stored persona pool is usually narrower than the audience a decision is about — read the distribution before targeting by id, and prefer describing the audience you want in thesia_plan_study when the pool does not match it.
tools.name: thesia_list_audiences
tools.title: List your simulated audiences

tools.description: Create simulated-audience personas to simulate against. Describe who you want to model and get back personas (with ids) you can then target as the 'audience' in thesia_audit_site, thesia_test_copy, or thesia_ask_audience. With pack_name the personas are also saved as an audience pack whose id thesia_run_study accepts. These are SIMULATED personas (engine-generated), not real people. Larger audiences can take a few minutes: the call then returns a job_id to pass back to collect them.

brand_context.description: Optional. The brand under test and its competitors, so personas carry brand awareness for that market. Requires segments or website_url; otherwise it is rejected.

category.description: Optional. The product category these people buy in (e.g. 'bottled water', 'wine gifts'). It describes what they shop for, never their job.

count.description: How many simulated personas to create (1-25, default 3).

description.description: Who to simulate, in plain language (e.g. 'price-sensitive first-time SaaS buyers in Germany' or 'busy parents shopping for groceries online'). When provided, Thesia engine-generates personas matching it; omit for a general-consumer audience.

job_id.description: Only to collect an audience that was still generating: pass the job_id an earlier call returned. Creates nothing new and bills nothing.

language.description: Optional. Language for the personas, e.g. 'ro'.

market.description: Optional. The country every persona lives in, as a name or ISO code (e.g. 'Romania', 'RO', 'DE'). Personas are placed in that country's cities.

max_wait_seconds.description: How long to wait inline before handing back a job_id. Defaults to 45.

pack_name.description: Optional. Name for the saved audience pack.

segments.description: Optional. Audience segments (max 12); weights follow 'size'. Give each segment occupations, locations, interests or goals and they are used exactly as written. With only a label and description, Thesia writes those details from your words, so the people fit the segment.

brand_awareness.description: How familiar this segment is with the brand.

goals.description: What they are trying to get done.

interests.description: Interests and traits, e.g. ['Bulk buying', 'Compares unit prices'].

key.description: Stable id for the segment, e.g. 'loyal_buyers'.

locations.description: Where they live, e.g. ['Bucharest', 'Voluntari']; the market is added when a country is missing.

occupations.description: Jobs these people hold, e.g. ['Teacher', 'Warehouse worker', 'Homemaker']. Without them the job is a generic professional one.

relationship_to_brand.description: Free text, e.g. 'switched to a competitor last year'.

website_url.description: Optional. A site to infer the audience from — Thesia analyzes it and generates personas that match its likely visitors.

tools.name: thesia_create_audience

inMarket.description: How many of the personas live in the requested market.

jobId.description: Pass as job_id to collect a 'running' audience.

packId.description: Saved audience pack id; pass it as 'audience' to thesia_run_study.

tools.title: Create a simulated audience
